readback.name: Poincare.FiniteAtlasBufferedTensorValue.weighted_transition
readback.mathematical_statement: Let E3 be EuclideanSpace R (Fin 3), the real three-dimensional Euclidean vector space. For every universe u, let M : Type u have a topology, an E3 charted-space structure, and the C-infinity IsManifold structure for the boundaryless closedSmoothModelWithCorners 3, at the ENat top injected into WithTop ENat. Let A : AtlasData M, with its finite extended-chart family C_j, subordinate open covering regions whose closures lie in genuine chart sources and have compact coordinate images, and smooth partition of unity p_j. No Hausdorff, CompactSpace, connectedness, metric, or time variable is explicitly assumed. Let xi be an arbitrary chart-indexed family of total scalar functions E3 -> R and W an arbitrary chart-indexed array of scalar functions W_jcd : E3 -> R, with c,d : Fin 3. The pinned definition V_iab(x) = value A xi W i a b x is p_i(x) times the finite sum over every source-chart index j of the following term: if x is in source(C_j), the term is xi_j(C_j(x)) times the double sum over c,d : Fin 3 of J_ij(x)_(c,a) * J_ij(x)_(d,b) * W_jcd(C_j(x)); otherwise the term is zero. The indicator is explicitly @ite R with Classical.propDecidable, so off-source total-chart values are excluded. Here J_ij(x)_(c,a) = jac A i j x c a = (fderiv R (C_j composed with C_i.symm) at C_i(x), applied to Euclidean basis vector e_a)_c. The transition direction is i coordinates to j coordinates, with output coordinate c and input coordinate a. All products and sums are ordinary real scalar arithmetic. Only destination partition p_i is inserted; there is no extra source partition p_j factor. No smoothness, compact support, range bound, cutoff-one condition, symmetry, spatial support, overlap law, or Graph hypothesis is imposed on xi or W by the definition. For every pair of destination chart indices i,k, every component indices a,b : Fin 3, and every x lying in both source(C_i) and source(C_k), one has p_k(x) * V_iab(x) = p_i(x) * the double sum over p,q : Fin 3 of J_ik(x)_(p,a) * J_ik(x)_(q,b) * V_kpq(x). This is the weighted covariant two-tensor transition equation for the actual defined finite source sum. The coordinate transformation used in this equation is i to k, and the same reconstructed value is transformed in both component slots. It is asserted for entirely arbitrary source arrays W and scalar buffers xi; the hypotheses do not supply compatible tensors, a separate cocycle package, or already compatible source fields. The direct imported module contains the genuine-chart Jacobian cocycle used by this construction, with its actual-source restrictions. The theorem does not cancel either partition or assume either is nonzero, so it retains the weighted equation even at zero partition values. The membership conditions are on x in the two genuine destination chart sources; the source-chart indicator inside every summed contribution continues to enforce its own chart-source condition. No unweighted transformation law, inverse partition, norm estimate, time scope, derivative certificate, or membership in a parabolic tensor carrier is asserted by this declaration.

Only destination partition p_i is inserted; there is no extra source partition p_j factor. No smoothness, compact support, range bound, cutoff-one condition, symmetry, spatial support, overlap law, or Graph hypothesis is imposed on xi or W by the definition. Assume the source arrays are pointwise symmetric: for every source-chart index j, component indices a,b : Fin 3, and every z in E3, W_jab(z) = W_jba(z). Then for every destination-chart index i, component indices a,b, and every x in M, V_iab(x) = V_iba(x). This conclusion covers all x without a chart-source membership premise, and no additional condition on xi is needed. It asserts symmetry of the actual finite buffered, destination-partition-weighted sum, rather than taking symmetry of that sum as an input. It does not assume any source transition compatibility and imposes no regularity or support requirement on W beyond the explicit pointwise symmetry. The declaration is a spatial scalar-array symmetry statement. It does not by itself construct bounded Graph operators, prove full X_M carrier membership or parabolic derivative estimates, establish a global DeTurck identity or contraction, or produce physical Ricci flow or Hamilton convergence.
